title: Edge Slice Quant-Fallback and Probe Preservation Manual
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Summary:
This manual defines the policy, operational procedures, and test artifacts for evaluating model slices intended for edge (on-device or near-edge) execution, while preserving probe semantics and enabling automatic quant-fallback to higher-precision variants in Redwood deployments. It covers: the probe preservation contract, slice-level fidelity checks, quant-profile configuration, orchestration patterns for fallback between edge and cloud, and a step-by-step regression triage runbook.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce release risk for quantized edge slices by ensuring behavioral parity on critical probe families and safe automated fallback when degradation is detected.
- Scope: Applies to all production model promotions tagged with "edge-ready" and any canary/production shadow runs that route traffic to edge-quant variants. Includes private/dedicated and hosted modes where edge-slice routing is configured.

Definitions:
- Slice: A workload segmentation (by tenant cohort, prompt family, context-length bucket) used in eval and rollout.
- Probe: A synthetic or captured input used to assert functional or safety properties (e.g., financial-parsing probes, instruction-following anchors).
- Probe preservation: Property that quantization or prompt-rewrite transformations do not change the probe's acceptance-class (PASS/WARN/FAIL) and core entity outputs beyond thresholds.
- Quant-fallback: Automated routing of requests from a quantized edge variant to a higher-precision cloud variant when quality or latency conditions are violated.

Owner and responders:
- Primary owner: Applied ML - Quant team (oncall: quant-oncall rotation)
- Secondary owner: Runtime infra team (oncall: runtime-oncall rotation)
- Pager escalation: See incident matrix in related_pages.

Fidelity gates (must pass before canary):
1) Probe Preservation Gate (automated):
   - For each slice, run the canonical probe set (N >= 250 per slice) against the candidate quantized variant and the baseline fp16/float model.
   - Metrics collected: PASS rate, semantic edit distance (SED), embedding cosine delta, functioncall argument diff-rate.
   - Gate thresholds (default):
     - PASS rate >= 98% relative to baseline OR absolute PASS >= 96%
     - Median SED <= 0.03 for instruction-following slices
     - Embedding cosine delta median >= 0.985 for semantic-preservation slices
     - Functioncall arg diff-rate <= 1.5%
2) Latency/Cost Gate:
   - p95 latency on-device must meet slice SLO or quant-fallback policy must be enabled.
   - Unit token cost for edge variant must be <= baseline cost * 0.7 to justify deployment.
3) Safety/Privacy Gate:
   - Any probe that triggers a safety sentinel (e.g., hallucination classifier) must have no increase in false-positive or false-negative rates > 0.5% absolute.

Quant profile example (YAML snippet):
---
quant_profile: edge-small-8bit-v1
target_bits: 8
per_channel: true
layer_exceptions: ["output_projection", "lm_head"]
kv_cache_preserve: true
prompt_rewrite:
  enabled: true
  max_tokens_rewrite: 64
fallback_policy:
  enabled: true
  threshold: 0.015  # semantic delta threshold to trigger fallback
  backoff_seconds: 30
  priority: ["same-region-higher-precision", "nearest-dedicated"]
---
Notes:
- layer_exceptions list should be minimized; more exceptions reduce memory savings.
- kv_cache_preserve avoids recomputing cache shapes and is required for long-context slices.

Probe preservation contract (engineer-facing):
- Provide a probe bundle with: 1) canonical inputs, 2) expected golden outputs (structured JSON where applicable), 3) labels for PASS/WARN/FAIL, and 4) a short rationale for each probe family.
- The eval harness will run: baseline -> candidate quant -> rewrite-candidate (if prompt_rewrite enabled). The triad enables attribution of regressions to rewrite vs quant steps.

Orchestration patterns for quant-fallback:
- Policy-driven routing: Requests are routed to edge-quant variant by default. Router evaluates telemetry in-flight (local fast checks) for explicit fallback signals:
  - FAST signals (local): immediate mismatch with small golden sentinel, token-level confidence drop > 0.2, or functioncall failure. Triggers immediate synchronous fallback.
  - SLOW signals (telemetry): aggregated semantic-delta over 1 minute > threshold (configurable), increases in user-reported error rates. Triggers adaptive ramp-down and canary rollback.
- Graceful fallback modes:
  1) Synchronous fallback: reroute the request to cloud, return cloud result. Use when safety or immediate correctness is critical.
  2) Asynchronous re-eval: return edge result but schedule a re-eval against cloud for telemetry. Used for non-blocking UX flows.
  3) Progressive throttling: reduce fraction of edge traffic when slow signals occur until baseline metrics recover.

Observability and telemetry requirements:
- Telemetry payload (per request): {slice_id, probe_id_if_probe, latency_ms, tokens_in/out, semantic_delta, embedding_cosine, functioncall_status, safety_flags}.
- Aggregation windows: 10s, 1m, 5m for fast detection; daily for drift analysis.
- Dashboards to include: slice-level PASS rate, semantic_delta distribution, p95 latency, fallback-rate, and cost-per-token.
- Alerts (examples):
  - ALERT_EDGE_QUANT_SEMANTIC_SHIFT: when 1m aggregate semantic_delta>threshold for >3 consecutive windows. Severity: P1.
  - ALERT_EDGE_FALLBACK_SPIKE: fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 5m. Severity: P2.

Runbook: regression triage flow (when ALERT_EDGE_QUANT_SEMANTIC_SHIFT fires)
1) Triage (first 10m):
   - Owner: quant-oncall. Acknowledge alert, attach current canary id and slice ids.
   - Query: use eval-harness replay to run 1k recent probe exemplars across baseline, candidate, and rewrite-candidate.
   - Quick check: compare PASS rate deltas; if delta > 5% absolute, escalate to oncall runtime.
2) Containment (10-30m):
   - Enable progressive throttling to 10% for affected slices or enable synchronous fallback for safety-critical slices.
   - Start a shadow traffic replay (non-blocking) to collect richer artifacts.
3) Diagnosis (30-90m):
   - Run attribution matrix: split regressions by probe family, prompt_rewrite impact, layer exception suspects, and context length.
   - If problem localizes to rewrite: disable prompt_rewrite for that slice and re-evaluate.
   - If problem localizes to quant: generate candidate with modified layer_exceptions and re-run canary.
4) Remediation (90m-24h):
   - Preferred fix: hotfix quant profile and push new edge artifact through canary.
   - If fix requires model change: rollback to previous quant bundle or pin traffic to baseline cloud variant and schedule a patch release.
5) Post-incident (24h-7d):
   - Create a regression report: root cause, artifacts, metrics before/after, and owners.
   - Add new probes to probe bundle if the regression exposed blindspots.

Canary and rollout policy (slice-aware):
- Canary fractions: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% over minimum 24h with 2 monitoring gates at 2% and 10%.
- Canary stop conditions:
  - Any safety sentinel increase > 0.2% absolute.
  - PASS rate delta > 2% absolute vs baseline.
  - Fallback rate > 1% sustained for 30m for latency-sensitive slices.

Examples: CLI and eval-harness commands
- Run probe bundle locally (example):
  $ ri-eval run --bundle ./bundles/edge-payment-probes.json --variant edge-small-8bit-v1 --baseline fp16 --slice slice_financial_parsing --out results.json
- Compare results with quick diff tool:
  $ ri-eval diff --baseline results_baseline.json --candidate results.json --metrics pass_rate,semantic_delta,embed_cosine --report /tmp/regression-report.html
- Trigger controlled fallback (ops):
  $ ri-router set-fallback --slice slice_financial_parsing --policy synchronous --priority same-region-higher-precision --duration 60m --reason "Emergency fallback due to semantic shift"

Testing checklist before promotion:
- [ ] Probe preservation gate passed for all release slices (N probes >= 250 per slice)
- [ ] Latency SLOs validated on representative devices/emulators (p95 measured)
- [ ] Cost-per-token estimates reviewed and justified
- [ ] Safety sentinels baseline/OLAP checks passed
- [ ] Canary playbook scheduled with monitoring owners assigned

Appendix A: Example probe schema (JSON lines)
{"probe_id": "edge-pay-001", "slice_id": "slice_financial_parsing", "input": "Extract transaction amount from: 'Charge $12.99 to card ending 4242'", "golden_output": "{\"amount\": 12.99, \"currency\": \"USD\"}", "label": "PASS", "rationale": "Canonical numeric extraction case for payments flow"}

Change log:

Notes and rationale:
- The manual favors conservative fallbacks for safety-critical slices (payments, identity) and progressive throttling for low-risk UX flows to balance costs and user impact.
